lang.name: English
welcome.title: Check your iPhone for known spyware
welcome.lead: Connect your iPhone with a cable. BugBane compares its system records with published fingerprints of known spyware and stalkerware. It usually takes 10 to 30 minutes, and nothing from your iPhone leaves this Mac.
learn.1.b:
Spyware is a hidden program that secretly copies what's on your phone (messages, photos, location, passwords) and sends it to someone else. You usually can't see it: no icon, no notifications.

  • Stalkerware is sold to ordinary people, often a jealous partner or an over-controlling parent. It usually needs your passcode or Apple Account password to be set up.
  • Mercenary spyware (like Pegasus) is sold to governments. The most advanced kinds can break in without you tapping anything, but they're very expensive and aimed at a small number of people: journalists, activists, politicians, business leaders.
learn.2.b:
Security researchers (Amnesty International, Citizen Lab, Google, Kaspersky, Lookout and others) publish the fingerprints of the spyware they catch: the names of its hidden programs, the web addresses it talks to, the files it leaves behind.

Your iPhone keeps its own records: which programs ran, what crashed, when it restarted, which websites loaded. BugBane copies those records to this Mac and compares them with thousands of published fingerprints.

It's like a blood test: it looks for the known signs of known illnesses. A clear result is reassuring, but no test finds every illness.
learn.3.b:
• Apps: where each one came from, and whether any is a known spy or monitoring app.
  • Settings profiles and VPNs: hidden settings that could let someone control the phone or reroute your internet traffic.
  • The programs running now, and lists of programs from the past few days.
  • The restart log. Pegasus was famously caught this way.
  • Crash reports and system logs. Break-in attempts often cause crashes and leave messages behind.
  • In a full check: links in your messages, the websites you visited, and which apps used the internet.

No person reads your messages or sees your photos. The software only compares names and web addresses with the fingerprint lists.
learn.4.t: What this check can't tell you
learn.4.b:
• A clear result means no known spyware was found. It doesn't mean the phone is safe. Brand-new spyware without published fingerprints can be missed, as with every tool, including the ones experts use.
  • Restarting the iPhone removes some spyware and its traces. That's good for you, but it means an older infection may leave nothing to find.
  • BugBane checks the phone, not your accounts. If someone knows your Apple Account password, they can read your iCloud data without touching the phone. The results show how to check that too.
  • Some findings are false alarms, for example a visit to the website of a company that also makes a monitoring app. Each finding says how likely it is to matter.
learn.5.b:
• Everything stays on this Mac. Nothing about your iPhone is uploaded or shared with anyone, including the people who make BugBane. There's no sign-up, no analytics and no trackers.
  • The copy of your iPhone is erased automatically when the check ends.
  • Only if you choose to, the result (not your data) is saved in History on this Mac. You can delete it at any time.
  • At the end, this Mac forgets your iPhone, so it can't connect to it again without your permission.
  • Only check a phone that is yours, or one whose owner has clearly agreed. Checking someone else's phone without permission is wrong, and illegal in many countries.
  • If you think a partner or family member is spying on you, removing their app can alert them. Talk to a domestic-violence helpline first: they can help you stay safe.
privacy.title: How BugBane handles your data
privacy.lead: To check your iPhone, BugBane reads sensitive records from it. This is what happens to them.
privacy.c.own: This is my iPhone, or its owner is here and agrees to this check.
privacy.c.process: I agree that BugBane processes the data on this iPhone, on this Mac, only for this check and as described above.
privacy.c.history: Save the result in History so I can open it again later.
privacy.error: Tick both required boxes to continue.
notice.title: Privacy notice
notice.body:
Who processes the data

{operator} (“we”), using the BugBane software on this Mac.

What data

Data read from the connected iPhone: device information (name, model, iOS version), the list of installed apps and configuration profiles, diagnostic records (running programs, crash reports, system logs, restart records), and in a full check an encrypted local backup (links in messages, browsing history, app network usage, permissions). Photos and videos are not analysed.

Purpose

Detecting signs of known spyware and stalkerware on your iPhone, at your request.

Legal basis

Your explicit consent (GDPR Article 6(1)(a) and, where the data reveal special categories of personal data, Article 9(2)(a)). You can withdraw your consent at any time by stopping the check; stopping erases the data collected so far.

Where

Only on this Mac. No data is transmitted to us or to any third party. No cloud, analytics or tracking.

How long

Raw data is erased immediately after the analysis. The result is kept only if you save it to History, until you delete it. If signs of spyware are found and you choose to keep the evidence for an expert, it stays on this Mac until you delete it. We keep an anonymous record of the date and time consent was given, with no data about you or your phone.

Your rights

Access, erasure, restriction of processing, and the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority (in Hungary: the Nemzeti Adatvédelmi és Információszabadság Hatóság, naih.hu).

Contact

{contact}
connect.title: Connect your iPhone
connect.s1: Plug your iPhone into this Mac with a cable (USB-C or Lightning). Use a cable that carries data, not a charge-only one.
connect.s2: Unlock the iPhone with Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode, and keep it unlocked.
connect.s3: If a question appears on the iPhone, read on: the next screen shows what to tap.
connect.help: Nothing happening after 30 seconds? Try a different cable or USB port, and make sure the iPhone is unlocked.
trust.title: Tap “Trust” on your iPhone
trust.s1: A question appears on the iPhone: “Trust This Computer?”
trust.note: This lets this Mac read the iPhone's diagnostic records. BugBane removes this permission at the end of the check.
trust.waiting: Waiting for you to tap Trust…
trust.locked: Unlock your iPhone. The question only appears on an unlocked screen.
trust.denied: You tapped Don't Trust. Unplug the cable and plug it back in to see the question again.
svg.trust.b1: Your settings and data will be
ready.title: Choose a check
ready.multi: More than one iPhone is connected. Choose which one to check:
mode.full.b: Also checks links in messages, websites and app activity, using an encrypted backup. Needs free space on this Mac ({free} free).
mode.quick.b: Apps, profiles, VPNs, running programs, the restart log, crashes and system logs. Skips messages, websites and app activity, and makes no backup.
ready.note: Keep the cable connected until the end.
ready.pre.1: Keep the iPhone unlocked, plugged in and nearby until the end.
ready.pre.2: The iPhone will ask for its passcode to allow the backup. Enter it on the phone.
ready.pre.3: Keep this Mac plugged in with the lid open. It stays awake by itself during the check.
step.decrypt: Opening the backup on this Mac
explain.prepare: BugBane is getting the newest spyware fingerprint lists.
explain.apps: BugBane is listing every app and settings profile on the iPhone.
explain.crashes: BugBane is collecting crash reports. Break-in attempts often make apps crash.
explain.sysdiagnose: The snapshot is a detailed report the iPhone writes about itself: running programs, the restart log and system logs.
explain.backup: The backup lets BugBane check links in messages, websites and app activity. Photos and videos are skipped.
explain.decrypt: The backup is opened with its password, only on this Mac.
explain.analyze: Everything is compared with the fingerprints of Pegasus, Predator, DarkSword, stalkerware and more.
explain.report: The result is being written in plain language.
d.sys.preparing: Your iPhone is preparing the snapshot. This takes 5 to 10 minutes.
d.sys.timeout: The snapshot didn't arrive in time. The check continues without it.
d.sys.copying: Copying the snapshot to this Mac…
d.backup.nopw: Skipped: without the backup password, everything except the backup is checked.
d.backup.nokeychain: Skipped: BugBane couldn't store a temporary password safely on this Mac, so it didn't change the iPhone's backup setting. Every other check still runs.
d.backup.unplugged: The iPhone was disconnected, so the backup stopped. An interrupted backup can't be checked. Reconnect the iPhone and start the check again.
d.backup.passcode: Your iPhone may ask for its passcode. Enter it on the phone.
d.backup.copying: Backing up… keep the cable connected.
d.backup.lowspace: Stopped: this Mac is almost out of space. The other checks still run.
d.backup.failed: The backup didn't finish. Check the cable and keep the iPhone unlocked.
d.decrypt.done: {n} files opened, photos and videos skipped
d.analyze.mvt: Checking links in messages, websites and app activity…
d.analyze.logs: Searching the system log (this takes a few minutes)…
p.press.title: Press three buttons on your iPhone
p.press.text: Press Volume Up, Volume Down and the Side button together for about 1 second, then let go. You'll feel a short buzz and may see the screen flash.
p.press.tip1: Don't hold them longer than 1–2 seconds. Holding brings up the power-off and Emergency SOS screen. If that happens, let go and don't slide anything.
p.press.tip2: BugBane notices automatically. The iPhone then needs 5–10 minutes to write the snapshot.
p.pw.title: Enter this iPhone's backup password
p.pw.text: This iPhone protects its backups with a password, chosen when “Encrypt local backup” was turned on in Finder or iTunes. BugBane keeps it in memory only for this check.
p.pw.forgot_text: You can skip the backup part: every other check still runs. To remove a forgotten backup password for next time, on the iPhone go to Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Reset > Reset All Settings. This resets settings such as Wi-Fi passwords and wallpaper, not your photos, messages or apps.
p.passcode.title: Enter your passcode on the iPhone
p.passcode.text: Your iPhone may ask for its passcode to allow the backup. Enter it on the phone.
rs.title: Finish restoring your iPhone's backup setting
rs.body: An earlier check ({model}, {date}) was interrupted. For the backup, BugBane had turned on encrypted backups with a temporary password, and turning it off again didn't happen. The password is kept in this Mac's Keychain, so BugBane can finish the job.
rs.connect: Click Start a check and connect this iPhone: as soon as it's connected, you can switch the setting back here. If the Mac no longer recognises it, run a check (a Quick check is enough): BugBane restores the setting at the end.
rs.btn_note: Your iPhone may ask for its passcode.
rs.working_b: Look at your iPhone: if it asks for your passcode, enter it on the phone.
rs.done: Done: your iPhone's backups are back to how they were (not encrypted).
rs.failed: That didn't work. Make sure the iPhone is connected and unlocked, then try again.
rs.failed_locked: Your iPhone is locked. Unlock it, then try again.
rs.failed_timeout: The iPhone didn't respond. If it asked for its passcode, enter it on the phone, make sure the phone is unlocked, and try again.
rs.other_b:
On this Mac: open Keychain Access, search for “BugBane” and copy the password. Then in Finder, select the iPhone, untick Encrypt local backup and enter that password.
On the iPhone: Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Reset > Reset All Settings. This removes the backup password, and also resets settings such as Wi-Fi passwords and wallpaper. It doesn't touch your photos, messages or apps.
rs.dismiss_confirm: This also deletes the saved temporary password. Only do this if the iPhone's backups are no longer encrypted with it.
p.space.title: This Mac might run out of space
p.space.text: The backup needs about {need} of free space (only databases are kept, not photos or videos). This Mac has {free} free. BugBane stops safely if space runs low.
run.title: Checking {name}
run.stop_confirm: Everything collected so far is erased from this Mac.
v.ok.b: BugBane compared this iPhone's records with {total} published spyware fingerprints. None matched. No check can rule out brand-new spyware, or spyware that ran only in memory and was removed by a restart.
v.warn.b: Some apps or settings could give someone else access to this iPhone, or need an update. Each item marked Worth a look says whether it's likely fine and what to do.
v.alert.b: Something on this iPhone matches a published spyware fingerprint. An expert can confirm what it is. Until then, don't reset, update or restart the iPhone.
v.partial.t: No known spyware in what BugBane could check
res.clean_b: BugBane looks for known spyware only. Brand-new spyware without published fingerprints can be missed, and spyware that lives only in memory disappears when the phone restarts. The fingerprint lists include {families}, plus stalkerware and monitoring apps.
sup.link: Something not working? Open the support log
sup.title: Support log
sup.lead: If something went wrong, send this file with your support request. It contains no data from your iPhone: no name, no identifiers, no apps, no messages. You can read all of it below before you send it.
res.forget: Make this Mac forget this iPhone (recommended)
next.update: Keep iOS up to date in Settings > General > Software Update. Updates fix the flaws spyware uses.
next.restart: Restart your iPhone every few days. A restart removes some spyware that runs only in memory.
next.safety: Run Safety Check in Settings > Privacy & Security > Safety Check, to see who can see your location and data, and which devices are signed in to your Apple Account.
next.password: Change your Apple Account password if anyone else might know it, and make sure two-factor authentication is on.
next.lockdown: If your work or public profile could make you a target, turn on Lockdown Mode in Settings > Privacy & Security > Lockdown Mode.
next.warn: Read each item marked Worth a look. It says whether it's likely fine and what to do. If someone you know may have set it up, talk to a domestic-violence helpline before you remove anything.
next.alert1: Don't reset, update or restart the iPhone yet. That can erase the evidence an expert needs.
next.alert2: Keep the collected data (choose below) so an expert can review it.
next.alert3: Get free, confidential help from the Access Now Digital Security Helpline (accessnow.org/help), for journalists, activists and people at risk.
next.alert4: If a partner or family member might be behind it, contact a domestic-violence helpline in your country before you remove anything.
next.alert5: Use a different device to talk about this until it's resolved.
data.erased: The copy of this iPhone has been erased from this Mac. Nothing from the phone was kept.
data.keep_t: Keep the collected data for an expert?
data.keep_b: BugBane hasn't erased the collected data yet, because an expert may need it. It stays only on this Mac. If you keep it, the result is saved in History, where you can erase the evidence at any time.
data.kept: The collected data is kept on this Mac for an expert. You can erase it from History at any time.
data.erase_confirm: An expert won't be able to review it. The result on screen stays until you finish.
done.title: Finished
done.erased: Everything collected from the iPhone has been erased from this Mac.
done.forgot: This Mac is no longer one of the iPhone's trusted computers.
done.saved: The result is saved in History.
done.unplug: You can unplug the iPhone now.
hist.title: History
hist.lead: Results saved on this Mac. Only the result is stored, never the iPhone's data. Anyone who uses this Mac account can open them.
hist.empty: No saved results. After a check, choose Save to History to keep the result here.
off.b: You can close this window. To check again, open BugBane.
quit.confirm: A check in progress stops, and its data is erased.
token.t: Please open BugBane from its app icon
token.b: This page needs the private link the app opens for you.
chk.apps.title: Installed apps
chk.apps.what: Every app installed on the iPhone, where it came from (the App Store or somewhere else), and which ones have special powers such as running a VPN or monitoring Screen Time.
chk.apps.tail.warn: A few apps are worth a look.
i.apps.ioc: “{name}” matches the known monitoring or spy app “{malware}”. If you didn't install it, don't remove it yet: removing it can alert whoever installed it. Follow the steps under What to do next first.
i.apps.sideload: “{name}”: not installed from the App Store. Apps installed this way skip Apple's review. Fine if it's from your employer or you're a developer; suspicious if you don't recognise it.
i.apps.testflight: “{name}”: a TestFlight beta app. Fine if you joined that beta.
i.apps.screentime: “{name}”: can use Screen Time controls (see and limit app use). Normal for parental-control apps. Make sure you know who set it up.
i.apps.vpn: “{name}”: can run a VPN or filter internet traffic. Fine if you installed it.
chk.profiles.title: Settings profiles and remote management
chk.profiles.what: “Configuration profiles” are settings packs that can control an iPhone: install certificates, reroute traffic, or let an organisation manage the phone remotely (MDM). Stalkerware for iPhone often relies on one.
i.profile: Installed profile: “{name}” (from {org}). If it isn't from your school or work, or something you set up yourself, remove it in Settings > General > VPN & Device Management.
chk.network.title: VPN and internet filters
chk.network.what: VPNs, DNS settings and web filters decide where your internet traffic goes. A hidden one could send everything you do online through someone else's server.
chk.network.none: No VPNs, filters or custom DNS.
i.net.heavy: “{name}” is set up as: {kinds}{profile}. This can see or redirect your traffic. Fine if you or your employer set it up; otherwise remove it.
i.net.vpn: VPN configured: “{name}”. Fine if you installed it.
chk.processes.title: Programs running right now
chk.processes.what: A list of every program running on the iPhone at the moment of the snapshot, checked against the names used by known spyware and against the folders where genuine iPhone programs live.
i.proc.ioc: A running program ({name}) has the same name as a program of known spyware ({malware}).
i.proc.implant: A program is running from a hidden system folder where spyware has been found before. Genuine iPhone programs don't run from there.
i.proc.odd: A program is running from an unusual location.
i.proc.unresolved: {n} system program(s) didn't report their location; none of them matches a known spyware name.
chk.jetsam.title: Program lists from the past few days
chk.jetsam.what: When the iPhone runs low on memory, it writes down every running program. These notes go back several days, so they can catch spyware that ran earlier.
chk.jetsam.skip: No memory reports were found on the phone.
i.jetsam.ioc: “{name}”: matches a program name of known spyware ({malware}).
chk.shutdown.title: Restart log
chk.shutdown.what: Each time the iPhone restarts, it notes which programs were slow to close. Pegasus-style spyware has been caught this way (the “shutdown.log” method).
chk.shutdown.skip: No restart log in the snapshot.
chk.shutdown.empty: The log is empty (the phone may have been reset or updated recently).
i.shut.ioc: A program with the name of known spyware ({malware}) delayed a restart.
i.shut.implant: A program from a hidden system folder delayed a restart, a known sign of Pegasus-style spyware.
i.shut.odd: A program from an unusual location delayed a restart.
i.shut.empty: The restart log is empty, so older infections can't be checked this way.
chk.crashes.title: Crash reports
chk.crashes.what: Hacking attempts often make apps crash first. BugBane looks for the crash patterns left by known iPhone attack kits, and for crashes from programs that shouldn't exist.
chk.crashes.skip: No crash reports on the phone.
i.crash.sign: “{name}” crashed in a way that matches a known attack kit (DarkSword). One crash can be a harmless bug; many in a row are suspicious.
i.crash.ioc: A crash came from a program whose location or name is linked to spyware.
i.crash.burst: {n} crashes of messaging, web or media programs within one hour ({hour}). Attack attempts often look like this.
chk.logs.title: System log search
chk.logs.what: The iPhone's system log (millions of lines), searched for the exact messages and files left behind by the 2026 DarkSword and Coruna attack kits and other known spyware.
chk.logs.skip: No system log in the snapshot.
chk.logs.timeout: The log search took too long and was stopped.
i.log.hit: The system log contains a message left by a known attack kit.
chk.mvt.title: Messages, websites and app activity (MVT)
chk.mvt.what: Amnesty International's Mobile Verification Toolkit (MVT) checks the backup: links in your text messages and iMessages, websites, which programs used the internet, privacy permissions and more, all against the fingerprint lists.
chk.mvt.skip: No backup was checked (a quick check, or the backup was skipped).
chk.mvt.sum: {total} records checked ({sms} messages, {web} websites, {usage} app network records).
hit.merc.msg: A message on this phone contains a web address used in spyware attacks ({malware}). Don't open it. Leave the phone as it is and contact an expert (see What to do next).
hit.merc: A trace that matches professional spyware ({malware}). An expert needs to review it. Don't reset the phone yet.
hit.stalk.web: Probably harmless: the app itself isn't installed. A browser loaded a website belonging to the maker of the monitoring or parental-control app “{malware}”. That usually just means one of the company's pages, ads or trackers loaded. Worth a closer look only if someone else has had your phone.
hit.stalk.web.vendor: Probably harmless: {malware} isn't installed. A browser loaded a website of {vendor}, which makes {malware} and also {products}. Using one of those, or opening one of the company's pages, ads or trackers, is the usual reason. Worth a closer look only if someone else has had your phone.
hit.stalk.web.also: The same finding as above: a website of the maker of “{malware}”.
hit.stalk: A sign of a monitoring app (“{malware}”). Apps like this can track messages and location. If you didn't set it up yourself, someone may be watching this phone. Before you remove anything, read What to do next: removing it can alert whoever installed it.
chk.browsers.title: Browsing history
chk.browsers.what: Your browsing history, checked against web addresses used by spyware. MVT reads Safari and Chrome; BugBane adds Firefox, whose newer history file MVT misses.
chk.browsers.nohist: No additional browser history to check.
chk.ios.title: iOS updates
chk.ios.what: Apple fixes the security flaws spyware uses in iOS updates. An up-to-date iPhone is protected against the publicly known attacks.
i.ios.update: iOS {latest} is available; this phone runs iOS {ios}. Update in Settings > General > Software Update.
chk.nosnapshot: Not checked: there's no diagnostic snapshot.
rep.title: iPhone check: {name}
rep.help_b: Free, confidential help for journalists, activists and people at risk: the Access Now Digital Security Helpline, accessnow.org/help. If a partner or family member may be monitoring you, contact a domestic-violence helpline before you remove anything, because removing it can alert them.
rep.generated: Report generated by BugBane on this Mac. It contains no data copied from the iPhone beyond the findings listed above.
err.no_device: Your iPhone isn't ready yet. Check the cable and that the phone is unlocked, then try again.
err.generic: BugBane couldn't do that. Check that the iPhone is connected and unlocked, then try again.
i.apps.remote: “{name}”: a remote-access app. Once you start it, someone else can see your screen. Tech-support scammers often ask people to install apps like this. Remove it if you don't use it.
d.backup.retry: The iPhone stopped the backup, usually because the passcode wasn't entered in time. Trying again…
rail.label: Steps
welcome.l.looks.b: Stalkerware and monitoring apps, hidden settings profiles and VPNs, and government spyware such as Pegasus, Predator and DarkSword
welcome.l.compares.b: Your iPhone's own records with thousands of published spyware fingerprints
welcome.l.keeps.b: Nothing from your iPhone. The copy is erased when the check ends.
welcome.limit: No check can prove a phone is free of spyware. BugBane tells you whether it found signs of known spyware.
privacy.l.read.b: The lists of apps and settings profiles, diagnostic records (running programs, crash reports, system logs, the restart log) and, in a full check, an encrypted backup: links in messages, browsing history and app network use. Photos and videos are skipped. Software compares names and web addresses; no person reads your messages.
privacy.l.change.b: This Mac becomes one of the iPhone's trusted computers until the check ends. If the iPhone's backups aren't encrypted, BugBane turns encryption on for the check with a temporary password, keeps that password in this Mac's Keychain, and turns encryption off again at the end.
privacy.l.online.b: Nothing about you or your iPhone. BugBane only downloads the public spyware fingerprint lists and Apple's public list of iOS versions.
privacy.l.stays.b: Nothing from the iPhone: the copy is erased when the check ends or when you stop it. A backup password you type is kept only in memory. The result is saved only if you choose History below.
privacy.c.history_sub: Only the result, not the iPhone's data. Anyone who uses this Mac account can open it.
p.press.skip_cost: The checks that need the snapshot won't run: running programs, the restart log and the system log.
p.pw.label: Backup password
p.pw.help: This is not the passcode you use to unlock the iPhone.
run.calm: Nothing to do right now. Stay near your iPhone.
run.free: BugBane won't need you again for this check.
run.m.buttons: Press three buttons on the iPhone
run.m.passcode: Enter the passcode on the iPhone
run.tip: Keep the cable connected. Don't restart or update the iPhone during the check.
res.provenance: The fingerprint lists include {families}, plus stalkerware and monitoring apps.
hist.confirm_erase_t: Erase the evidence kept for this result?
hist.confirm_erase: An expert won't be able to review it. The result stays in History.
rep.method: BugBane {version} compared the iPhone's records with published spyware fingerprints (exact matches only). Each finding names the check that raised it and the evidence it was based on.
v.partial.fix.snapshot: The diagnostic snapshot is missing. To include it, run the check again and press the three buttons when BugBane asks.
v.partial.fix.backup: No backup was checked. To include it, run a full check again and let the backup finish.
v.partial.fix.other: Under All checks, each one says why.
chk.apps.none: No apps installed apart from Apple's own.
